feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy expertise. It reads professionally and is well structured, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope, leadership, and ownership of digital strategy, platforms, and operations.  
- Good credibility through concrete platform/tool references and scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Writing is polished and audience-appropriate, with a strong summary and consistent focus on mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, process efficiencies, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead. No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one clearer positioning statement and tighter, more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of cross-channel leadership.
- Add public-sector/advocacy context to better match the experience section.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, noun-based phrasing and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership strengths over lower-level tasks like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web & CMS modernization • Editorial systems & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, align terms with strongest evidence in recent roles: enterprise web, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and multimedia production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and several other items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim; consider keeping only one skills-style section.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by foregrounding 2–3 distinctive outcomes/projects and reducing generic channel/governance language.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate bullets around distinct contributions: enterprise workflows/analytics; Drupal campaign builds; AI search initiative. Avoid listing every channel.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholder teams served.
- Tighten phrasing, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits; improved CMS workflows, front-end performance, and troubleshooting for public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the summary and NACo roles.
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” is broad and overlaps with core competencies unless tied to a concrete result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter, bullets started with outcomes, and channel-management points were less generic and less repetitive with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national public-sector association.”
- Tighten and sharpen bullets to emphasize scale + transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email engagement, audience growth, campaign performance, production volume, or cost/time savings if available; otherwise cut “tens of thousands/thousands” as too vague.
- Rephrase operations bullets for impact: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video/studio language may duplicate the footer’s “Advocacy Video Series” project.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than clearly scoped leadership. Tighten it around operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with clearer ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet for impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more concrete: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.” Add metrics if possible: send volume, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating governance language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier NACo role and footer project list; distinguish this role as the scaling/operational phase.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented, higher-seniority skills:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and campaign planning
- Consider replacing “messaging” with “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- “Content operations” is stronger than “content planning” because it aligns with governance, workflows, and systems shown in recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, add a measurable qualifier in experience instead of here (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” already echo the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with NACo Director and Associate Director bullets; keep this section concise rather than repeating detail.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented skills summary. In this topline section, emphasize current strengths tied to recent work and modernization leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing, with the strongest/current items first.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences • SharePoint, Power Pages and WordPress • Airtable-based content systems”
- Drop “jQuery” here unless it is still central to current work; it feels dated for a topline summary.
- Use “Airtable-based content systems” or “content operations systems” to sound more strategic and less tool-specific.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this version high-level and let the technical section carry the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep it only if it remains a clear differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making value, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, and performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than listing each as separate bullets.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider rewrite as: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every analytics tool here if they already appear in the Technical section; use this space to signal senior-level capability.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent leadership-level capabilities rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia, Studio & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, more senior phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: **Built and operated an in-house broadcast-quality studio for advocacy programming and event coverage**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the Core Competencies line **“Multimedia production and livestream operations”**; use this item for more specific sub-skills, not the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “livestreaming” are already evidenced in recent NACo experience, so keep this concise and non-repetitive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or removed to save space.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recentest relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If keeping this section, add proficiency/context rather than just names, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and better alignment with the rest of the CV.
- Best option: trim lower-signal tools if space is tight, e.g. **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**, since GitHub Pages is less central to the recent leadership narrative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists the same core platforms.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects, so repeating the full list without context adds little value.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize current implementation tools and group them more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & tagging:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager • **Deployment & edge tooling:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Use consistent taxonomy: replace “Coding & Technical Implementation” with **Front-End, Integrations & Deployment** for clearer scope.
- If accurate, add specificity instead of more tools: e.g., “REST API integrations,” “event tagging in GTM,” or “CI/CD workflows in GitHub Actions.”
- Consider dropping versioned labels like HTML5/CSS3 unless the rest of the CV also uses versioning; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding adjacent automation terms here unless they are distinct.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize system-building, not just apps: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if Basecamp/Trello are older or lighter-use, consider dropping them.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier tied to impact: “Used to streamline editorial planning, cross-team coordination and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same language elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; include only if they supported notable operational systems, not basic communication.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent roles. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation/customer journeys)** • **Mailchimp (email marketing)**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 director role, put that first; if Mailchimp was older/light use, keep it last or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this item tool-focused and leave audience size/volume in experience.
- “Engagement” is broad; avoid repeating multi-channel language already covered in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Keep it focused on foundational contributions and early leadership, not broad channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of video updates, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the closing clause: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervising/mentoring a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and weekly video content while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier buildout/launch phase.
- Avoid repeating broad ownership of web/email/social, which is already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts” so it adds distinct value without overlapping too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope + standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the rest into one impact-oriented clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one metric or concrete output: number of episodes, audience growth, projects supported, or types of materials delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry more focused on innovation/research support and the podcast as a first.
- Avoid broad “supporting organizational programs and policy work” unless you can specify project types or stakeholders.
